bullets.text: I learned that **Making Tax Digital (MTD)** for Income Tax will significantly change how landlords and sole traders manage their tax submissions, starting from April 2026.
I found out that under **MTD for Income Tax**, landlords will no longer need to submit annual Self Assessment tax returns, but instead will provide quarterly updates using compatible software.
I discovered that **MTD for Income Tax** aims to improve financial visibility for businesses, allowing them to better manage their cash flow and tax liabilities throughout the year.

I noted that the first phase of **MTD for Income Tax** will apply to those with income over £50,000 starting in April 2026, with subsequent phases lowering the threshold to £30,000 and £20,000 in 2027 and 2028, respectively.
I learned that good financial record keeping is essential for landlords in the UK, as it helps ensure compliance with tax obligations and maximizes income.
I found that **MTD for Income Tax** is part of the UK government's broader initiative to digitalize the tax system, which began with **MTD for VAT** in 2019.
I discovered that the **Let Property Campaign** was introduced by HMRC to encourage landlords to declare rental income and pay the correct amount of tax, as many fail to do so.
I noted that **MTD for Income Tax** will require landlords and sole traders to use software to keep digital records and submit regular updates to HMRC, enhancing efficiency.
I learned that the transition to **MTD for Income Tax** is seen as a major shift in tax management, potentially benefiting millions of sole traders and landlords in the UK.
I found that the introduction of **MTD for Income Tax** is expected to reduce administrative burdens for businesses, allowing them to focus more on growth and customer service.
